case_title: MAHAVIR SINGH v. STATE OF HARYANA
aggravating_circumstances: Conspiracy, opportunity to commit murder, grievous injuries
neutral_facts: The accused and co-accused were seen with the victim on a specific date. The victim was later found dead in a canal. The body was recovered several days later, and a post-mortem was conducted. The medical report indicated the victim had sustained grievous injuries. Evidence included recovered items such as the victim's chappal, blood-stained clothing of the accused, and a blade with blood traces. The prosecution alleged that the accused and co-accused conspired to kill the victim at the instance of the victim's wife. The accused and co-accused were convicted of murder and other charges. The courts below found the circumstantial evidence complete and the accused had the opportunity to commit the crime.
